output.title: Table extraction is only the first checkpoint
output.body:
Table extraction is useful, but it is only the first checkpoint. If you stop at pulling line items into a sheet, the real work is still waiting: who checks the data, what rule decides the next action, and what gets logged for later review. That is where a lot of manual effort sits.

For a small business owner, the better question is not “can we extract the table?” It is “what happens after extraction, and does that step repeat under a clear rule?” If there is no repeated decision, extraction alone may be enough. If there is, you may have a bounded workflow worth automating.

A practical example is a back-office flow that flags duplicates, applies a simple amount rule, records the decision, and hands control back to a human before any money moves. Human approval stays mandatory for high-risk decisions. Three-way matching is not built here, so keep the scope narrow.

Bareni’s working policy is no-lock-in: finished code is handed over, and the customer’s database, automation-tool accounts, and API accounts are in the customer’s name from the start. If you want a quick test, write down the step after extraction, the rule it follows, and the time it costs you each week.
